chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
I asked him about the fingers: Are they equal in the blood money (diyah)? He said: Yes.

key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: blood money / compensation for bodily injury

ai.seo_question: Are all fingers valued equally in Islamic blood money compensation?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) confirms the equality of all fingers in the payment of blood money (diyah), a ruling foundational to Shia jurisprudence on bodily compensation. This consensus simplifies the complex calculations of injury compensation by removing distinctions between individual digits, reflecting the principle of uniformity in physical integrity. The ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on clarity and accessibility in legal rulings derived directly from the Imams.
